title: brag-bridge
angle: A developer has a real project but wants a launch film without moving the codebase into a hosted video service. The film follows one object—the local project—from source code to ChatGPT's MCP workflow to a rendered MP4, showing brag-bridge as the local execution bridge: ChatGPT plans the creative work while the desktop binary reads files and runs Hyperframes/ffmpeg. The visual world is a crisp terminal-and-code workspace, with real command names and source excerpts from this repository; no invented dashboard or unsupported performance claims.
tone: polished — premium developer-tool launch film; precise, confident, quietly technical

palette.name: Creative direction: deep terminal navy (no app stylesheet or brand palette in this CLI project)
Creative direction: electric blue for the local-to-creative handoff

music_notes: This brag-bridge build ships no bundled music or SFX, as confirmed by README.md and list_assets. The film will be intentionally silent; rhythm comes from performed type, cursor actions and transitions.

scenes.name: The output first
scenes.script: A launch film. From your codebase.
scenes.visual: Open on a real terminal/editor workspace. A rendered brag.mp4 output is visible as the payoff object, then the camera pulls back to reveal the brag-bridge repository and its Go source. Use real filenames README.md, main.go and tools.go; no fake product UI.
scenes.motion: The output filename slams in on frame one; per-word blur reveal lands the second line. A fast camera pull-back reveals the workspace, then the MP4 rectangle becomes the carrier into the next scene.
scenes.transition_out: whip-pan — the MP4 output streaks horizontally and resolves as the terminal prompt in the next scene

scenes.name: The local bridge
scenes.visual: Show the real README command `brag-bridge serve --tunnel` in a terminal, then a readable excerpt from README.md explaining that the local binary reads files, writes compositions and runs Hyperframes and ffmpeg. Highlight the actual MCP boundary, not an invented dashboard.
scenes.motion: The command types and executes in the terminal; the camera punches into `--tunnel`, then the terminal surface expands to become a clean code-reading world. Keep the exact command and explanatory copy still once settled.
scenes.transition_out: iris from the command — the `serve` token becomes the aperture into the MCP tool registry

scenes.name: The real workflow
scenes.visual: Show the actual tool registrations from tools.go, one at a time: `brag_guide`, `project_tree`, `submit_plan`, `approve_plan`, `hyperframes`, `finalize`. A focused code view proves these are real MCP tools. Pair it with the documented two-phase flow from README.md: plan is locked until approval, then local composition and render.
scenes.motion: A cursor traces the real tool names in the source excerpt; each name resolves into a single prominent verb. A restrained camera pan follows the source lines, then a zoom-through on `approve_plan` carries into the build result. No fabricated counts or dashboard widgets.
scenes.transition_out: zoom through `approve_plan` — the highlighted identifier expands into the rendered composition workspace

scenes.name: Rendered locally
scenes.visual: Show the documented local render path and real output artifacts from the existing brag workflow: `composition/`, `brag.mp4`, `brag.jpg`, `share-copy.txt`. These are the actual deliverables described by the README and workflow; avoid implying cloud rendering.
scenes.motion: The composition folder assembles from the source view; the MP4 tile travels across the frame and settles centre. A brief camera push lands on `brag.mp4`, then pulls back to show the local output directory.
scenes.transition_out: colour flood — the deep terminal ground brightens to the end-card blue while the MP4 tile stays anchored

scenes.name: The handoff
scenes.visual: Minimal end card built around the product name and a terminal-style CTA: `brag-bridge serve`. This is a documented CLI command, not a website URL. No logo asset exists in the project tree, so the wordmark is set in type rather than pretending an icon is the brand mark.
scenes.motion: The wordmark assembles letter by letter, locks to centre, then the CLI command wipes on beneath it. Hold the final lockup for the full beat.

share_copy: brag-bridge connects ChatGPT to a local project so it can inspect the code, plan a launch video, and run Hyperframes + ffmpeg on your machine. ChatGPT does the creative work; your desktop does the building.
avoid: No invented dashboard, UI, metrics or speed claims
No implication that source code or renders are uploaded to a hosted build service
No tiny floating screenshots or three-card feature slides
No typing-prompt opener, repeated fade-up entrances or docked logo
No music or SFX: this build ships no bundled audio
